question: Which permanent tools.fs policy contract should OpenClaw support, and should v1 explicitly exclude exec-mediated access or require a real process sandbox for exec?
rationale: The competing config shapes, compatibility semantics, and security claims cannot be safely selected by an automated repair, and parsing arbitrary shell commands would not form a reliable boundary.

options.title: Canonical file-tool policy
options.body: Choose one tools.fs path-policy contract for native file/media tools and document that exec requires sandboxing or denial.

options.title: Full process boundary
options.body: Design the feature around an OS or container sandbox that constrains both native file tools and arbitrary child processes.

options.title: Keep workspace-only model
options.body: Decline granular host-path policy and continue directing operators to workspaceOnly, dedicated OS users, VMs, or containers.

recommendation.title: Canonical file-tool policy
recommendation.body: Choose one tools.fs path-policy contract for native file/media tools and document that exec requires sandboxing or denial.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current workspace-only guard and participated in the existing maintainer-side issue decision trail.
